rule: Lines of one colour on a single background. Pure-diagonal chains are cells linked by diagonal steps whose two corner cells are background. All non-root chain cells are erased. The root is the chain cell with exactly one orthogonal foreground neighbour. A ray runs straight from the root, away from that neighbour. If the ray hits a line cell, the background it crosses is filled with the line colour. If it leaves the grid, the root is erased too. Rootless loose diagonals are erased. Plain gaps stay open.

authored_scope: Random scenes: 12..30 per side by default, explicit sizes 10..30. Any pair of distinct colours. 1..3 row lines and 1..3 column lines with edge, crossing or free ends. Each scene has 1..3 collinear bridged gaps (length 2..5, weighted to 3), 1..2 plain gaps and 0..2 loose or near-miss diagonals. Optionally it has a perpendicular stub whose ray exits the grid (erased, as in the test fixture) or hits a parallel line (filled, a synthetic extension). Optionally it has a staircase on a free line end whose ray completes a T-junction or exits the grid and erases the end cell (a synthetic extension). Not supported: multiple line colours, noise, staircases that lean away from the gap (they cannot form a valid chain), rays that cross plain gaps, and order-dependent ray interactions. Explicit mode reproduces the fixtures from latent objects. It checks shape and bounds but not ambiguity.
authored_constraints: Pure-diagonal adjacency in the input equals exactly the intended chain links
Each root has exactly one orthogonal foreground neighbour; non-root chain cells and loose cells have none
Filling rays cross only background, are pairwise disjoint and end on a non-erased line cell
Non-gap filling rays and erasing rays never cross plain or bridged gap cells or other fills
Erasing rays reach the grid edge through untouched background
Foreground density at most 40% so background is the majority colour
Line positions at least 3 apart; collinear gaps reserve a 2-cell margin on each side
At least one collinear bridged gap and one plain gap per random scene
Background and line colour differ; all controls are genuine ints within range

diversity_audit.method: Input-derived diagonal graph and simultaneous straight rays

original_audit.rule: One background colour plus horizontal and vertical lines in one colour, with some gaps. Pure-diagonal chains are cells joined by diagonal steps whose two shared corner cells are background. Every chain cell except the root is erased. The root is the chain cell with exactly one orthogonal foreground neighbour. From each root, a ray runs straight away from that neighbour. If the ray hits a foreground cell, the background cells it crossed are filled with the line colour. If it leaves the grid, the root is erased as well. Gaps without a staircase stay open.

findings.location: generate(), explicit branch: `if None in (width, height, background, color)` / `if not diagonals`
findings.issue: The module docstring says 'Diagonals/bridges/stubs without lines are rejected'. However, lines=[] is not None, so it takes the explicit branch. Nothing checks that lines is non-empty, so a grid with diagonals and no lines is accepted. The output is a scene where every piece is loose and nothing is repaired.
findings.suggested_fix: In the explicit branch add `if not lines: raise ValueError('explicit scenes need at least one line')`, or reword the docstring.
findings.test: generate(width=10, height=10, background=0, color=5, lines=[], diagonals=[(2,2,1,1,2)]) returns a grid today; per the docstring it should raise ValueError.

findings.location: _sample_scene(): 300 outer attempts x len(plan) (up to 9 kinds) x 40 _propose/_check retries
findings.issue: Each _check rebuilds fg and scans all foreground cells. On the smallest allowed random grids (10 per side), the 40% foreground cap and the 3-apart line spacing reject many candidates. That could mean close to 100k _check calls before RuntimeError, possibly several seconds per call. The docstring admits RuntimeError for small sizes but gives no time bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure wall time and failure rate at width=10/height=10. If either is high, cap the total proposals per outer attempt, or scale the line count to the grid size.
findings.test: Time 5 calls of generate(width=10, height=10). Report the success rate and the maximum latency; expect both to stay within the host budget.

findings.issue: A plain gap starting at a+1, or ending at b-1, leaves a one-cell remnant at the line end. If that end is a free point rather than the grid edge or a crossing, the scene contains a floating isolated pixel. The fixtures only show one-cell segments touching the grid edge, ((v,4,0,0) and (h,9,23,23)). The reference leaves such a pixel untouched, so the output is still correct. It is, however, a visually novel stub-like distractor that the latent checks never consider.
findings.suggested_fix: Either require a remnant of at least 2 cells unless the end is a grid edge or crossing (lo = a + 2 when a is a free point), or document the isolated remnant as an intended distractor.
findings.test: Over 200 random scenes, count foreground components of size 1 that touch no grid edge. If any exist, decide whether they are intended.

findings.location: _propose(): kind 'bridge' (glen 2..5, k random 1..glen-1), kind 'gap' (glen 1..4), kind 'stub' with hit, kind 'end'
findings.issue: The fixtures only show these cases: bridged gaps of length 3 with a staircase of exactly glen-1=2 cells, one perpendicular stub whose ray leaves the grid, and loose diagonals of 2..3 cells. The generator adds bridge gaps of 2/4/5, staircases shorter than glen-1, plain gaps of length 1, perpendicular stubs that fill to a parallel line, and line-end staircases. Line-end staircases either complete a T-junction or erase a genuine line cell. These are labelled synthetic in the docstring and stay consistent with the reference transform. They are still extrapolations of the hidden rule; for example, the original task might tie staircase length to gap length.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep them, but consider a flag or reduced probability for the purely synthetic kinds ('stub' with hit, 'end'), so default samples stay close to fixture evidence.
findings.test: Tally the sampled kinds and the (glen, k) pairs over 200 scenes. Confirm that fixture-like (3, 2) bridges are a substantial share.

findings.issue: Explicit diagonals or stubs may overlap line cells; they are painted and then erased, which punches holes in lines. Explicit scenes are also not checked against the reference rule, for chain purity or ray direction. The docstring acknowledges this.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally run _check-like pure-diagonal and degree checks for explicit scenes, or keep this as documented host responsibility.
findings.test: generate(width=10, height=10, background=0, color=5, lines=[('h',4,0,9)], diagonals=[(4,4,1,1,1)]) succeeds and erases (4,4), which breaks the line in a way the reference would not produce.

findings.location: _positions(): `random.randint(1, n - 2)`; _sample_scene(): one line per row/column index
findings.issue: Lines never lie on the border rows or columns. Each row or column index carries at most one original line, so collinear segments arise only from gaps. Both fixtures and the test also respect this, so it is a diversity limit rather than an error.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: allow positions 0 and n-1 with low probability, only for line kinds that do not need perpendicular stairs room.
findings.test: Invariant: no random scene has foreground on row 0 except vertical lines or stubs (expected under the current code).

targeted_checks: For many random seeds, apply the supplied reference transform to the input and assert it equals the generated output. This is the main oracle, because _check mirrors the rule but is not the rule.

validate() fixtures: by inspection, pair 1 row 7, the pair 2 row-9/v18/v11 bridges and the test stub (15,2)+(16,3) all match the canonical grids. Host should confirm exact equality for all three grids.
In random scenes, assert exactly one foreground colour, and that the background is the strict majority colour of the input.
Assert that every staircase root has exactly one orthogonal foreground neighbour, and that each chain component has at most one such cell.
Assert that no fill ray (bridge, free ray) crosses a plain-gap cell, and that plain gaps remain background in the output.
Assert that each stub ray or end ray with no hit really reaches the grid edge through background in the post-erasure grid.
Check the colour-control paths: background-only, color-only and both, with distinct colours always honoured.
Measure latency and RuntimeError rate at width=10,height=10 and width=10,height=30.
